BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.
exchanges.text:
## Overall position

**Do not accept the Seller’s “FINAL” or principal-agreed characterisation.** It is not evidence of buyer authority. No required written approval from Amelia Frost has been given for the 20% cap or 18-month claims period. The asserted market practice does not override our playbook.

The draft materially weakens recovery rights and leaves important Completion protections unresolved. Its most significant structural problem is the proposal to apply general limitations to **all Claims**, potentially undermining separately negotiated title, tax, IP, payment and covenant protections.

## Material departures and recommended pushback

### 1. General warranty liability: restore our starting positions

| Issue | Seller position | Buyer response and reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| **Cap — clause 12.1** | 20% / AUD 4.8 million | Restore **25% / AUD 6 million**. The proposed cap reduces available protection by AUD 1.2 million. The 20% fallback requires Amelia’s prior written authority identifying the draft; none exists. |
| **Thresholds — clause 12.2** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket | Require **AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 aggregate tipping basket**, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. The Seller’s formulation excludes more individual claims and permanently leaves the first AUD 250,000 of otherwise qualifying losses with us. |
| **General claims period — clauses 12.3/13** | 18 months | Require **24 months after Completion**. Eighteen months is an approval-dependent fallback, not an agreed position. |
| **Claims-wide application** | Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded | Reject the default. Specify each regime’s scope and priority so general warranty limitations cannot silently restrict other rights. |

Any negotiated movement must be assessed as a package, but cannot be treated as authorised merely because it appears in this draft.

### 2. Fundamental/title protection and misconduct carve-outs

**Fundamental/title claims need their own regime:** a **100% cap, at least six years**, and exclusion from the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar. Administrative simplicity is not a sufficient reason to leave the buyer with only general warranty protection if the Seller lacks ownership or capacity to transfer the shares.

Clauses **9.3, 12.8 and 20.5** also need express, overriding carve-outs for **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**, to the maximum extent enforceable. Those matters must sit outside:

- all caps, baskets and time limits;
- exclusive-remedy provisions; and
- non-reliance provisions.

**This protection cannot be waived.** Check the entire agreement for provisions that could indirectly defeat it, rather than relying on a single isolated exception.

Keep title, tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants distinct. An indemnity or payment obligation should not inadvertently become a capped, time-barred general Warranty Claim through an expansive definition of “Claim”.

### 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**Reject general disclosures 1.1–1.2 as blanket warranty qualifications.** Require specific fair disclosure identifying the relevant matter and explaining its nature and scope sufficiently for the buyer to understand it. Uploading material to the data room, referring to statutory registers or making information publicly searchable is not a substitute.

Specific disclosures still need individual assessment. Their inclusion does not establish that the underlying risk has been resolved or that it should be accepted without protection.

**Delete clause 8.3’s blanket buyer/adviser knowledge exclusion**, including deemed knowledge of matters discoverable through searches. It would shift the risk of deficient disclosure to us and potentially defeat negotiated protection merely because an adviser could have found something.

Any permitted **seller-knowledge qualification** should identify named seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. Knowledge wording must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### 4. Bluefen: material Completion condition remains unsatisfied

Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6 million / 30% of FY26 revenue**. The disclosure expressly says there is no final consent or evidence that its associated conditions have been satisfied.

Require before Completion:

- effective written change-of-control consent;
- evidence that the conditions under clause 11.3 are satisfied; and
- confirmation that the consent is effective for this transaction.

**Reasonable endeavours and delivery of a consent letter are insufficient.** A delivered document may remain conditional or ineffective. The SPA should not deem this material condition satisfied merely on delivery.

### 5. Riverlark: repayment and security releases must be controlled

The approximately **AUD 3.2 million** balance is not a current payout figure. The facility remains unpaid and no final security discharge is supplied.

Require:

- a current payout statement;
- direct repayment from Completion funds; and
- effective releases of the relevant security, coordinated with Completion.

The proposed unsecured promise of a post-Completion release is unacceptable. Any post-Completion release mechanism requires **an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia’s approval**. Ensure the funds flow and debt-free/cash-free mechanics align, without double counting.

### 6. Employee bonuses: close the funds-flow gap

DD-005 identifies **AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses**, but the funds flow omits them. Calling these “a matter for the Seller” does not ensure the acquired company will not bear the cost.

Require an express line item or a documented seller-funded mechanism covering:

- bonuses actually triggered by Completion and continued-employment conditions; and
- applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other triggered on-costs.

Determine the on-cost treatment rather than assuming either that none apply or that a particular amount is payable. The funds flow must not silently leave this liability with the buyer.

### 7. Ironquay IP: broaden protection and verify the cure

The indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment is too narrow. The risk concerns ownership and use of the Project Materials, not merely payment of an invoice.

Broaden the indemnity to address losses arising from the identified ownership/transfer defect and its remediation, while preserving the **SOW3 cleared-payment cure**. Obtain evidence of cleared payment and appropriate confirmatory assignment/title documentation.

The **AUD 180,000 open balance is not independently verified**: it proves neither non-payment nor payment. Do not present that figure as an established liability or regard title as cured on the present record. IP terms remain open.

### 8. Export/privacy incident: investigate without prejudging the outcome

The Seller’s “not expected to be material” description is unsupported by the preliminary record. Equally, the disclosure does **not** establish a confirmed breach, unauthorised access, harm or a notification duty.

Require:

- preservation of relevant logs and evidence;
- investigation of access, actual export contents, scope and containment;
- continuing updates and provision of findings; and
- assessment of legal and contractual obligations against the established facts.

Retain appropriate pre-Completion information and conduct protections. Do not invent a loss amount, demand or automatic price adjustment; assess further protection as the investigation develops.

### 9. Sandbar renewals: assess before allocating the cost

Neither the Seller’s “ordinary-course” label nor automatic treatment as Debt is justified by the supplied information.

Review DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing, scope, accrual, termination rights and whether the commitments are unavoidable. Then determine the appropriate contractual and accounting treatment of the **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, avoiding double counting. **No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.**

### 10. Title evidence and remaining category-specific issues

- **Title evidence:** DD-012 is a supplied internal register, not independent proof of clean ownership or authority. Require independent ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence and reconcile it with the register and transfer documentation.
- **Tax/IP:** Reject the assertion that these positions are settled under the general regime. Both remain **open**; neither unlimited liability nor a resolved liability allocation should be assumed.
- **Office lease:** DD-007 identifies a **notification obligation**, not landlord consent. Verify and satisfy the actual notice requirement without inventing a consent condition.
- **Mossvale:** An assignment restriction does not, on the supplied wording, establish that a share sale requires consent. Review the complete contract for any separate change-of-control provision before concluding otherwise.

## Recommended negotiation priorities

1. **Restore the liability architecture:** 25% general cap, AUD 5,000/AUD 50,000 tipping thresholds, 24 months, separate fundamental/title protection and overriding misconduct carve-outs.
2. **Remove blanket risk transfers:** reject deemed disclosure, buyer/adviser knowledge exclusions and claims-wide general-regime overrides.
3. **Secure Completion:** effective Bluefen consent and satisfied conditions; current Riverlark payout, direct repayment and effective releases.
4. **Fix identified exposure:** expressly fund bonuses and on-costs; broaden Ironquay protection and verify the cure; investigate the incident.
5. **Keep unresolved matters genuinely open:** tax/IP allocation, Sandbar treatment and independent title verification.

Return the mark-up with these points expressly identified as outstanding—not as departures from an agreed buyer position.
